court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma

issues.label: Oklahoma jurisdiction to modify
issues.why: The court must confirm it has subject-matter and continuing exclusive jurisdiction to modify a Texas paternity/support order registered in Oklahoma.

issues.label: Valid registration of foreign order
issues.why: The court must ensure the Texas decree was properly registered and enforceable in Oklahoma before modification.

issues.label: Applicable uniform act framework
issues.why: The court must apply the correct interstate family-support regime (e.g., UIFSA/UCCJEA overlap questions) governing modification authority and procedure.

issues.label: Proper notice and service
issues.why: The court must confirm the motion to modify and fee application were properly served and noticed to satisfy due process.

issues.label: Material change threshold met
issues.why: The court must decide whether a substantial/material change in circumstances (including >25% income change) supports modification.

issues.label: Effect of 2021 agreed-order notice clause
issues.why: The court must interpret and enforce the provision requiring 7-day notice of >25% income increase and its consequence for modification.

issues.label: Self-executing modification validity
issues.why: The court must determine whether the 2021 clause allowing submission of new guidelines without a new motion is legally permissible and how it affects proceedings.

issues.label: Father’s noncompliance consequences
issues.why: The court must consider remedies for failure to disclose income changes (e.g., evidentiary inferences, sanctions, fees, retroactivity).

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must allocate burdens for proving income, guidelines amounts, and any deviation above the cap.

issues.label: Accurate current income findings
issues.why: The court must make supported findings on Father’s gross monthly income (including job changes, bonuses/commissions, variability) and Mother’s income.

issues.label: Income definition and inclusions
issues.why: The court must determine what earnings count as gross income under Oklahoma child support law (salary, bonuses, benefits, perquisites).

issues.label: Imputed income questions
issues.why: The court must decide whether to impute income to either parent (e.g., Mother’s earning capacity as lawyer, Father’s potential fluctuations) under governing standards.

issues.label: Parenting time/visitation impact
issues.why: The court must account for the custody/visitation arrangement (sole custody; supervised; minimal contact) in guideline inputs or deviation analysis.

issues.label: Child support guideline application
issues.why: The court must correctly apply Oklahoma’s child support guidelines to the extent the schedule applies.

issues.label: High-income case methodology
issues.why: Because combined income exceeds the schedule maximum, the court must select and apply the correct method for setting support above the cap.

issues.label: Archer v. Archer relevance
issues.why: The court must address controlling precedent for above-guideline/max-income support and explain any departure or distinguish Archer.

issues.label: Needs-based findings for children
issues.why: The court must evaluate evidence of the children’s reasonable needs and best interests, including direct and indirect expenses, when income exceeds guidelines.

issues.label: Standard of living consideration
issues.why: The court must consider whether and how the children should share in the higher standard of living available from Father’s increased income.

issues.label: Credibility and evidentiary support
issues.why: The court must resolve disputes over claimed expenses and make determinations supported by competent evidence rather than speculation.

issues.label: Father’s lack of expense knowledge
issues.why: The court must weigh Father’s limited contact and knowledge when assessing the credibility of his asserted lower expense estimate.

issues.label: Use of Father’s “offer” as basis
issues.why: The court must decide whether relying on Father’s volunteered amount (without guideline calculation/needs findings) is legal error or an abuse of discretion.

issues.label: Requirement for findings/explanation
issues.why: The court must provide sufficient findings or reasoning to permit appellate review, especially in a high-income/deviation context.

issues.label: Deviation from guidelines standard
issues.why: If the award deviates from the guideline amount, the court must satisfy statutory deviation requirements and articulate reasons.

issues.label: Cap-based proxy calculation issue
issues.why: The court must address whether using the guideline maximum schedule as a de facto cap is permissible when actual income far exceeds it.

issues.label: Evidence adequacy for Mother’s request
issues.why: The court must assess whether Mother’s expense documentation sufficiently supports the requested amount and how to treat mixed household expenses.

issues.label: Allocation of shared/indirect costs
issues.why: The court must determine proper attribution of housing, utilities, transportation, and other indirect costs to the children.

issues.label: Health insurance and medical costs
issues.why: The court must ensure medical insurance premiums, unreimbursed medical expenses, and allocation are handled per statute/order.

issues.label: Childcare/education expenses
issues.why: The court must consider any work-related childcare or education-related costs that should be added/allocated under Oklahoma law.

issues.label: Retroactivity of modification
issues.why: The court must determine the effective date of any modified support (filing date vs. later) and whether arrearage should be calculated.

issues.label: Support during job changes
issues.why: The court must decide how to treat Father’s income changes during the pending motion (averaging, stepped orders, or current income at hearing).

issues.label: Discovery compliance and sanctions
issues.why: The court must consider whether discovery abuses occurred and what sanctions/fee shifting are authorized and appropriate.

issues.label: Attorney-fee authority source
issues.why: The court must identify the specific statute or agreement authorizing attorney fees/costs in this parentage/support-modification context.

issues.label: Fee standard to apply
issues.why: The court must apply the correct legal standard for awarding fees (need/ability, equity, conduct, prevailing party, or statutory factors) under the applicable authority.

issues.label: Reasonableness of hours/rates
issues.why: The court must determine whether requested fees and costs are reasonable under lodestar-type factors and supported by evidence.

issues.label: Allocation/segregation of fees
issues.why: If awarding only discovery-related fees, the court must decide whether segregation is required and whether the chosen subset is justified and supported.

issues.label: Explanation for partial fee award
issues.why: The court must provide a rationale for awarding only discovery fees after finding the total request reasonable, to avoid arbitrary decision-making.

issues.label: Consideration of parties’ resources
issues.why: The court must weigh comparative ability to pay and financial condition, including Father’s high income and Mother’s income/expenses.

issues.label: Effect of settlement offers
issues.why: The court must determine whether and how refused settlement offers affect fee entitlement or amount under the governing statute/equity principles.

issues.label: Mother’s earning-capacity argument
issues.why: The court must decide if Mother’s potential return to law practice is relevant to fees (need/ability) and/or child support calculations.

issues.label: Causation of fees by misconduct
issues.why: The court must assess whether Father’s non-notice and discovery conduct caused additional litigation expense warranting fee shifting.

issues.label: Recoverable costs categories
issues.why: The court must determine which litigation expenses qualify as taxable costs or recoverable expenses under applicable law.

issues.label: Standard of review framing
issues.why: On review, the court must separate discretionary determinations from legal questions reviewed de novo (e.g., guideline interpretation, authority for fees).

issues.label: Weight-of-evidence assessment
issues.why: The reviewing court must determine whether the child-support amount is clearly against the weight of the evidence constituting abuse of discretion.

issues.label: Abuse-of-discretion in fee award
issues.why: The reviewing court must decide whether limiting fees to discovery without explanation is an abuse of discretion or legal error.

issues.label: Preservation/record adequacy
issues.why: The court must ensure issues were preserved and the record contains sufficient evidence and rulings to review support and fees decisions.
